subject.title: fix(exec): require approval for OpenClaw lifecycle commands

question: Should OpenClaw deliberately require explicit approval for non-yolo host-exec commands classified as gateway or daemon lifecycle mutations, even when an existing allowlist or auto-review path would otherwise permit them?
rationale: This is a policy choice that deliberately narrows existing non-yolo execution behavior and depends on an extensive command-classification taxonomy; source review cannot determine the intended long-term security and operator-automation tradeoff.

options.title: Adopt the scoped lifecycle interlock
options.body: Accept the stricter non-yolo approval contract, preserve the documented full/off yolo exception, and require a rebase plus exact-head validation before merge.

options.title: Narrow the policy surface
options.body: Limit the new mandatory approval rule to a maintainer-approved set of lifecycle entry points and leave broader shell-carrier classification out of the initial policy.

options.title: Keep current policy
options.body: Decline the new exception and close the linked security-hardening direction without changing existing allowlist and auto-review behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt the scoped lifecycle interlock
recommendation.body: Accept the stricter non-yolo approval contract, preserve the documented full/off yolo exception, and require a rebase plus exact-head validation before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Low-confidence routing candidate based on recent exec-approval documentation maintenance; a security or exec-policy owner should make the final call.
